**Core stack for a Lagos Life-style open-world game:**

- **Game engine:** Unity (C#) is the best fit for beginners and mobile. Unreal Engine (C++/Blueprints) gives better graphics but is heavier. Godot is free and lightweight but weaker for large 3D worlds.
- **3D modeling:** Blender (free) for buildings, vehicles, characters, and props.
- **Character animation:** Mixamo for free rigging and animations.
- **Assets:** Unity Asset Store, Sketchfab, and Kenney.nl for placeholder or ready-made models.
- **Code editor:** Visual Studio or VS Code, plus Git/GitHub for version control.
- **Audio:** Audacity for editing and FMOD for in-game sound. Add Afrobeats-style music through licensed or original tracks.
- **Textures and UI:** Figma, Krita, or Photoshop.
- **Backend (if multiplayer or saves):** Firebase, PlayFab, or Photon.
- **Mobile builds:** Android Studio and the Android SDK.

**Features to learn:** character controller, vehicle physics, NPC AI (pedestrians, traffic), a mission system, an in-game economy, and save/load.

**Tip:** Start small, with one street, one car, and one mission, before building the full city. Open-world games take big teams years, so a tiny playable slice is the realistic first goal.

Do you want a learning roadmap for Unity, or are you aiming at mobile or PC? 1. **Weeks 1-3: C# basics.** Variables, functions, classes, lists. Use Microsoft's free C# docs or Brackeys-style YouTube tutorials.
2. **Weeks 3-6: Unity fundamentals.** Scenes, GameObjects, prefabs, physics, UI. Finish Unity Learn's "Essentials" and "Junior Programmer" pathways.
3. **Weeks 6-9: Player and camera.** Build a third-person character with movement, jumping, and a follow camera (Cinemachine). Add Mixamo animations.
4. **Weeks 9-12: Vehicles.** Use Unity's WheelCollider to drive a car. Add enter/exit car logic.
5. **Months 3-4: Blockout the world.** Make one Lagos street in Blender or with ProBuilder: danfo buses, kiosks, market stalls. Use Unity's NavMesh for pedestrians walking around.
6. **Months 4-5: Gameplay systems.** Mission/quest system, dialogue, money and inventory, save/load using JSON.
7. **Months 5-6: Polish.** Sound, UI, day/night cycle, traffic AI.
8. **Month 6+: Optimize and ship.** For mobile, reduce polygons, bake lighting, compress textures, and test on a low-end Android phone early.

**Rules of thumb:**
- Finish one tiny game first (like a driving or runner game) before attempting the open world.
- Use free assets as placeholders, then replace them later.
- Commit to Git daily.

I assumed mobile since it's the most common target for Lagos-style games. If you're building for PC, tell me and I'll adjust the optimization steps.  M Targeting both is very doable in Unity, since one project builds to PC and Android. The key is to design for mobile first, then scale up for PC.

**Adjustments to the roadmap:**

1. **Build for the weakest device.** Test on a low-end Android phone from Month 3 onward, not at the end. If it runs there, it runs on PC.
2. **Input:** Use Unity's new Input System so one set of actions maps to keyboard/mouse, gamepad, and touch controls (on-screen joystick and buttons).
3. **UI:** Use Canvas Scaler set to "Scale With Screen Size" and anchor everything, so menus fit phones and monitors.
4. **Quality tiers:** Make Low (mobile) and High (PC) settings. PC gets higher-resolution textures, longer draw distance, more traffic and pedestrians, and better shadows.
5. **Render pipeline:** Use URP (Universal Render Pipeline). It works on both and is the standard choice for cross-platform.
6. **Assets:** Keep models low-poly with LODs (Level of Detail), and use texture atlases. PC can swap in higher-quality textures later.
7. **World streaming:** Split the city into chunks that load as the player moves. This matters most on mobile memory.

**Extra tools:** Unity Profiler and Frame Debugger for performance, plus Unity Cloud Build or GitHub Actions for automated builds.

**Release:** Android via Google Play, and PC via itch.io first (easy) or Steam later.

Want me to break down how to set up the touch-and-keyboard input system next?

Yes! Here is the complete breakdown and implementation for setting up the unified **Touch-and-Keyboard Input System** for your Lagos open-world game across Mobile and PC.

All code has been created, modularized, and structured directly in your repository under `Assets/Scripts/`.

You can also test the live interactive input simulator (with a movable Lagos street character, Danfo minibus, virtual touch joystick, keyboard bindings, and Lagos horn audio):
👉 **[View the Live Lagos Architecture & Input Tester](https://antigravity.luch.dev/site/1eec1899-c7b1-4c17-8a41-faf6b18c0fa9/42629e47f0c1505981d836df/)**

---

### 1. The Core Architecture Principle: Input Abstraction

In cross-platform games, **never query hardware inputs (`Input.GetAxis` or keycodes) directly inside your character or car scripts**. 

Instead, use a central **[InputManager](https://github.com/marvel-fresh/core-stack-for-a-lagos-life-style/blob/main/Assets/Scripts/Input/InputManager.cs)** singleton:
```text
[Keyboard / Mouse / Gamepad] ──┐
                               ├──> InputManager.Instance ───> [PlayerController / CarController]
[Mobile Touch Joystick & UI] ──┘
```

Both your character controller and your Danfo bus read only from `InputManager.Instance.MoveInput`, `IsSprinting`, and `JumpTriggered`.

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Unity Setup Guide

#### Step 1: Set Up the Canvas Scaler
To ensure on-screen buttons fit both small 5.5" phones and widescreen monitors:
1. In the Hierarchy, create a **UI Canvas** (`GameObject > UI > Canvas`).
2. Set **Canvas Scaler**:
   - **UI Scale Mode:** `Scale With Screen Size`
   - **Reference Resolution:** `1920 x 1080`
   - **Screen Match Mode:** `Match Width Or Height`
   - **Match:** `0.5`

#### Step 2: Create the Virtual Joystick
1. Create a UI Image named `JoystickBackground` (anchor to **Bottom-Left**).
2. Create a child Image named `JoystickHandle` inside it.
3. Attach **[VirtualJoystick.cs](https://github.com/marvel-fresh/core-stack-for-a-lagos-life-style/blob/main/Assets/Scripts/Input/VirtualJoystick.cs)** to `JoystickBackground`.
4. Drag `JoystickBackground` to the `Background` field and `JoystickHandle` to the `Handle` field.
5. Set `Handle Range` to `64` and `Dead Zone` to `0.1`.

#### Step 3: Add Action Buttons (Jump, Sprint, Enter Danfo, Horn)
1. In the **Bottom-Right** of your Canvas, add UI Buttons for actions:
   - **Sprint Button:** Attach **[TouchActionButton.cs](https://github.com/marvel-fresh/core-stack-for-a-lagos-life-style/blob/main/Assets/Scripts/Input/TouchActionButton.cs)** (`Action: Sprint`, check `isHoldAction = true`).
   - **Jump Button:** Attach **[TouchActionButton.cs](https://github.com/marvel-fresh/core-stack-for-a-lagos-life-style/blob/main/Assets/Scripts/Input/TouchActionButton.cs)** (`Action: Jump`, `isHoldAction = false`).
   - **Interact / Enter Danfo Button:** Attach **[TouchActionButton.cs](https://github.com/marvel-fresh/core-stack-for-a-lagos-life-style/blob/main/Assets/Scripts/Input/TouchActionButton.cs)** (`Action: Interact`).
   - **Horn / Handbrake Button:** Attach **[TouchActionButton.cs](https://github.com/marvel-fresh/core-stack-for-a-lagos-life-style/blob/main/Assets/Scripts/Input/TouchActionButton.cs)** (`Action: Horn` or `Handbrake`).

#### Step 4: Third-Person Character Controller
1. On your player GameObject, add a `CharacterController` component.
2. Attach **[PlayerController.cs](https://github.com/marvel-fresh/core-stack-for-a-lagos-life-style/blob/main/Assets/Scripts/Player/PlayerController.cs)** and **[PlayerInteraction.cs](https://github.com/marvel-fresh/core-stack-for-a-lagos-life-style/blob/main/Assets/Scripts/Player/PlayerInteraction.cs)**.
3. Assign your Main Camera (or Cinemachine Brain) to `Camera Transform` so movement is camera-relative.

#### Step 5: Lagos Vehicle Physics (Danfo Minibus)
1. On your vehicle prefab, attach a `Rigidbody` and 4 `WheelCollider` objects.
2. Attach **[CarController.cs](https://github.com/marvel-fresh/core-stack-for-a-lagos-life-style/blob/main/Assets/Scripts/Vehicles/CarController.cs)** and **[VehicleEntryExit.cs](https://github.com/marvel-fresh/core-stack-for-a-lagos-life-style/blob/main/Assets/Scripts/Vehicles/VehicleEntryExit.cs)**.
3. **Danfo Stability Tip:** Set `centerOfMassOffset` to `(0, -0.6, 0)` in `CarController`—this keeps tall Danfo buses stable around sharp corners.
4. When entering a vehicle, **[MobileControlsToggle.cs](https://github.com/marvel-fresh/core-stack-for-a-lagos-life-style/blob/main/Assets/Scripts/Input/MobileControlsToggle.cs)** automatically swaps the on-screen walking buttons for driving controls (Gas, Brake, Steer, Handbrake, Horn).

---

### 3. Scripts Created in Your Project

| Script | Location | Responsibility |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **[`InputManager.cs`](https://github.com/marvel-fresh/core-stack-for-a-lagos-life-style/blob/main/Assets/Scripts/Input/InputManager.cs)** | `Assets/Scripts/Input/` | Merges Keyboard (WASD/Arrows), Gamepad, and Touch into unified read-only properties |
| **[`VirtualJoystick.cs`](https://github.com/marvel-fresh/core-stack-for-a-lagos-life-style/blob/main/Assets/Scripts/Input/VirtualJoystick.cs)** | `Assets/Scripts/Input/` | Normalized UI touch joystick with deadzone and drag clamp |
| **[`TouchActionButton.cs`](https://github.com/marvel-fresh/core-stack-for-a-lagos-life-style/blob/main/Assets/Scripts/Input/TouchActionButton.cs)** | `Assets/Scripts/Input/` | Tap and hold mobile touch buttons (Jump, Sprint, Interact, Horn) |
| **[`MobileControlsToggle.cs`](https://github.com/marvel-fresh/core-stack-for-a-lagos-life-style/blob/main/Assets/Scripts/Input/MobileControlsToggle.cs)** | `Assets/Scripts/Input/` | Platform auto-detection (`Application.isMobilePlatform`) & Walking/Driving HUD switcher |
| **[`PlayerController.cs`](https://github.com/marvel-fresh/core-stack-for-a-lagos-life-style/blob/main/Assets/Scripts/Player/PlayerController.cs)** | `Assets/Scripts/Player/` | Camera-relative character controller, smooth rotation, jumping & gravity |
| **[`PlayerInteraction.cs`](https://github.com/marvel-fresh/core-stack-for-a-lagos-life-style/blob/main/Assets/Scripts/Player/PlayerInteraction.cs)** | `Assets/Scripts/Player/` | Proximity detection for Danfo buses, kiosks, and street NPCs |
| **[`CarController.cs`](https://github.com/marvel-fresh/core-stack-for-a-lagos-life-style/blob/main/Assets/Scripts/Vehicles/CarController.cs)** | `Assets/Scripts/Vehicles/` | Lagos vehicle physics: WheelColliders, motor torque, handbrake & horn audio |
| **[`VehicleEntryExit.cs`](https://github.com/marvel-fresh/core-stack-for-a-lagos-life-style/blob/main/Assets/Scripts/Vehicles/VehicleEntryExit.cs)** | `Assets/Scripts/Vehicles/` | Smooth enter/exit transition, camera target swapping, and player hiding |
| **[`README.md`](https://github.com/marvel-fresh/core-stack-for-a-lagos-life-style/blob/main/README.md)** | Root | Complete project setup guide and 6-month roadmap |

### Summary of What Has Been Implemented & Saved

#### 1. Unified Cross-Platform Input Layer
- **[`InputManager`](https://github.com/marvel-fresh/core-stack-for-a-lagos-life-style/blob/main/Assets/Scripts/Input/InputManager.cs)**: Central singleton that normalizes Keyboard (WASD), Gamepad, and Touch into a single stream.
- **[`VirtualJoystick`](https://github.com/marvel-fresh/core-stack-for-a-lagos-life-style/blob/main/Assets/Scripts/Input/VirtualJoystick.cs)**: Smooth mobile drag joystick with configurable deadzones and clamp ranges.
- **[`TouchActionButton`](https://github.com/marvel-fresh/core-stack-for-a-lagos-life-style/blob/main/Assets/Scripts/Input/TouchActionButton.cs)**: On-screen buttons for Jump, Sprint, Interact, Handbrake, and Horn.
- **[`MobileControlsToggle`](https://github.com/marvel-fresh/core-stack-for-a-lagos-life-style/blob/main/Assets/Scripts/Input/MobileControlsToggle.cs)**: Automatically shows/hides mobile touch UI based on the device, and toggles between Walking and Driving layouts.

#### 2. Locomotion & Lagos Vehicle Physics
- **[`PlayerController`](https://github.com/marvel-fresh/core-stack-for-a-lagos-life-style/blob/main/Assets/Scripts/Player/PlayerController.cs)**: Camera-relative third-person character locomotion with Cinemachine support.
- **[`PlayerInteraction`](https://github.com/marvel-fresh/core-stack-for-a-lagos-life-style/blob/main/Assets/Scripts/Player/PlayerInteraction.cs)**: OverlapSphere proximity detection for Danfo buses and street kiosks.
- **[`CarController`](https://github.com/marvel-fresh/core-stack-for-a-lagos-life-style/blob/main/Assets/Scripts/Vehicles/CarController.cs)**: 4-WheelCollider vehicle physics with lowered Center of Mass for stable Danfo handling, handbrake drift, and Lagos horn audio.
- **[`VehicleEntryExit`](https://github.com/marvel-fresh/core-stack-for-a-lagos-life-style/blob/main/Assets/Scripts/Vehicles/VehicleEntryExit.cs)**: Transitions the player into and out of vehicles, swaps follow cameras, and toggles mobile HUDs.

#### 3. Core Gameplay Systems
- **[`DanfoMissionManager`](https://github.com/marvel-fresh/core-stack-for-a-lagos-life-style/blob/main/Assets/Scripts/Missions/DanfoMissionManager.cs)**: Passenger pickup and drop-off route logic (Oshodi, Ojuelegba, CMS Marina).
- **[`EconomyManager`](https://github.com/marvel-fresh/core-stack-for-a-lagos-life-style/blob/main/Assets/Scripts/Economy/EconomyManager.cs)**: In-game Naira (₦) wallet for fares, fuel, and vehicle maintenance.
- **[`PedestrianAI`](https://github.com/marvel-fresh/core-stack-for-a-lagos-life-style/blob/main/Assets/Scripts/AI/PedestrianAI.cs)**: NavMesh sidewalk crowd behavior for busy Lagos market streets.
- **[`README.md`](https://github.com/marvel-fresh/core-stack-for-a-lagos-life-style/blob/main/README.md)**: Full project documentation, canvas scaling guides, and the 6-month roadmap.

Everything is committed to your repository and saved.
